=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:30-49 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `compute_autofix_iteration` can undercount or stop early in shallow git histories, causing `IS_FIRST_ITERATION` to be set incorrectly.
  WHY: All reviewers identified that `git log -1 --format='%s' "HEAD~${autofix_count}"` depends on complete history and returns empty/error at the shallow boundary, which makes the script fall back to iteration 1; severity was not explicitly stated by all reviewers, so the highest stated severity among them is medium.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:217-231 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new git-history-based iteration detection changes behavior from diff-file-based detection and can misclassify whether a run is the first iteration.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed this is a behavior change that can treat runs as iteration 1 when HEAD is not an `[ai-autofix]` commit or when prior state was previously inferred from the diff file; severity disagreement is resolved at the highest stated severity, medium.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:253-276 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The ledger-parsing scoping block is fragile because it assumes well-formed tab-separated input and has limited validation around malformed ledger content.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers flagged that the `awk` block can silently skip or misparse data when the ledger format is unexpected, which can leave scoping empty or incorrect; severity disagreement is resolved at the highest stated severity, low.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:272-276 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `sort -u` step lacks explicit error handling.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed the command can fail without a dedicated fallback, though they differed on impact; severity disagreement is resolved at the highest stated severity, low.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:220-224 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: `AUTOFIX_ITERATION` is compared numerically without guarding against non-numeric input.
  WHY: The reviewer reported that an invalid string value can trigger shell numeric-comparison errors before the fallback computation runs, so this remains a standalone input-validation bug.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:244-249 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The scoping logic uses `HEAD~1` semantics that may be misleading in merge-commit scenarios.
  WHY: This reviewer flagged that first-parent comparison can produce incorrect file scoping when HEAD has multiple parents.
- README.md:environment variables table | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The newly introduced feature flags are not documented in the README environment-variable table.
  WHY: The reviewer flagged a discoverability/documentation gap for `REVIEW_REVIEWER_CHECKLIST_ENABLED` and `REVIEW_REVIEWER_ITERATION_SCOPING`.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:35-49 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The iteration counting logic can fail in shallow clones because `git log -1 --format='%s' "HEAD~${autofix_count}"` stops at truncated history.
  WHY: If `git log` returns empty at the shallow boundary, the loop breaks early and `IS_FIRST_ITERATION` becomes `true`, bypassing repeated-issue prevention.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:217-231 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `IS_FIRST_ITERATION` now depends on counting autofix commits in git history instead of checking diff-file existence.
  WHY: This behavior change can make reviewer behavior inconsistent, especially when the first run is inferred from an `[ai-autofix]` commit rather than the previous diff file state.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:253-276 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The scoping logic lacks robust validation for ledger parsing and sort failure handling.
  WHY: The `awk` script assumes tab-separated fields and the `sort -u` step could fail, which can silently affect iteration scoping.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:35-49 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The iteration counter assumes deep git history and breaks at shallow-clone boundaries.
  WHY: In a shallow repository, `git log -1 --format='%s' "HEAD~${autofix_count}"` returns an error or empty string, so `compute_autofix_iteration` falls back to `1` and disables repeated-issue prevention.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:13-39 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `AUTOFIX_ITERATION` is not validated before numeric comparison.
  WHY: Passing a non-numeric value can trigger shell integer-expression errors in `[ "${AUTOFIX_ITERATION}" -lt 1 ]` before the script can fall back to computed iteration detection.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:254-267 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The ledger parser assumes a hard tab-separated format with no pre-validation.
  WHY: Malformed ledger content can cause incorrect or empty scoping data, and the parser swallows errors with `|| true`.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:35-49 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The history-walking iteration counter is inefficient for long chains.
  WHY: Repeated `git log -1` subprocess calls are slower than a single filtered `git log` pipeline, though the reviewer rated this as low impact.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/review_ru_working_ers.sh:30-47 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `compute_autofix_iteration()` walks git history with `HEAD~N`, which breaks on shallow CI checkouts.
  WHY: When `git log` returns empty at the shallow boundary, the function returns `1` and incorrectly sets `IS_FIRST_ITERATION=true`, bypassing repeated-issue prevention logic.
- scripts/review_ru_working_ers.sh:~260-275 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The ledger parsing logic assumes well-formed tab-separated input and has no validation or error handling for malformed files.
  WHY: The `awk` block can silently skip or misparse entries if the ledger file structure changes or is corrupted.
- scripts/review_ru_working_ers.sh:~274-275 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `sort -u` step has no explicit failure handling.
  WHY: If `sort` fails, the scoped-files output may be empty or the command may fail silently.
- scripts/review_ru_working_ers.sh:~226-232 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Changing first-iteration detection from diff-file presence to git-history counting can alter reviewer behavior unexpectedly.
  WHY: Runs can be classified as iteration 1 or not based on commit-message history rather than prior diff-file state, which may not match existing workflows.
- scripts/review_ru_working_ers.sh:~16-28 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `normalize_feature_flag()` silently falls back to the default for invalid values.
  WHY: Invalid feature-flag strings are accepted without warning, which can hide configuration mistakes.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:217-231 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new iteration detection can misclassify a run as first iteration when HEAD is not an `[ai-autofix]` commit.
  WHY: The counter only walks backward from HEAD through `[ai-autofix]` commits, so a manual commit on top of an autofix chain can still be reported as iteration 1.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:35-49 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `compute_autofix_iteration()` depends on `HEAD~N` history that may be missing in shallow CI clones.
  WHY: Limited history can make `git log HEAD~N` fail or return empty, producing incorrect iteration counts and wrong `IS_FIRST_ITERATION` handling.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:253-267 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The ledger parser can silently produce incorrect scoping data when the input format is unexpected.
  WHY: The `awk` block has no format validation before filtering, so malformed ledger content can lead to empty or malformed scoped-file output.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:275-276 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `sort -u` step has no explicit error propagation.
  WHY: If sorting fails, the scoped-file output may be empty or partial without triggering a dedicated fallback.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:244-249 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The scoping logic may be wrong for merge commits because it uses `HEAD~1`.
  WHY: `HEAD~1` refers to the first parent, which may not be the relevant comparison point in merge workflows.

=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:30-47,223-233 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `compute_autofix_iteration` counts only consecutive `[ai-autofix]` commits from HEAD, so a non-autofix HEAD can still be misclassified as the first iteration.
  WHY: If HEAD is a manual commit on top of prior autofix work, the function returns `1`, which makes the reviewer run full-diff instructions instead of scoped review.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:30-47 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The loop-based history walk is fragile in shallow clones.
  WHY: `git log HEAD~N` fails beyond the shallow boundary, causing the loop to break early and undercount autofix iterations.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:272 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `sort -u` command has no guard and can abort the whole script under `set -e`.
  WHY: An I/O or permissions failure in `sort` stops the reviewer workflow instead of falling back safely.
- README.md:environment variables table | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new feature flags are not documented in the README environment-variable section.
  WHY: `REVIEW_REVIEWER_CHECKLIST_ENABLED` and `REVIEW_REVIEWER_ITERATION_SCOPING` are used in the script but not described in the documented configuration surface.
